title: Cannot Print
cardText: Diagnose a printer that does not print when a job is sent.
Check printer error messages, print queues, connections, drivers and network access.
Identify whether the problem is with the printer, computer, application or network.
text: This guide is for printers that do not print after a document is sent from a Windows computer.
Start by checking the printer's status messages and error codes.
Test whether the printer can print independently before investigating Windows.
Then check the selected printer, print queue, connection and driver.
Follow the relevant troubleshooting steps for USB or network printers.

checkPrinterStatus.title: Check printer status
body: Look at the printer's display or status lights.
Check for messages such as Paper Jam, Out of Paper, Replace Toner, Ink Empty, Cover Open or a specific error code.
Follow any instructions displayed on the printer.
The printer should be in a Ready state before continuing.

resolvePrinterError.title: Resolve printer error
body: Follow the error message shown on the printer.
Load paper, remove jammed paper carefully, close covers or replace consumables as needed.
Use the manufacturer's instructions when clearing paper jams to avoid damaging internal components.
If an error code remains, look it up using the exact printer model.
Once the printer returns to Ready, test it again.

link.name: Microsoft printer troubleshooting
link.description: General Windows printer troubleshooting, including printer errors and connections.

printerHardwareFault.title: Printer hardware fault or servicing required
body: The printer has an error that cannot be cleared through normal troubleshooting.
Record the exact printer model and error message or code.
Check the manufacturer's support instructions for that error.
If the error persists, the printer may require repair or replacement.

printerSelfTest.title: Can the printer print its own test or configuration page?
body: If supported, use the printer's control panel to print an internal test, configuration or status page.
The exact menu varies by model. Look under Settings, Reports, Information or Maintenance.
This test should run without sending a document from Windows.
If the internal page prints, the printer mechanism is probably working and the issue may involve the computer or connection.
If the internal page fails, investigate the printer itself before changing Windows settings.

checkCorrectPrinter.title: Check the selected printer
body: Open the document's Print dialog.
Confirm the correct physical printer is selected.
Check that the job is not being sent to Microsoft Print to PDF, OneNote, an old printer or another device.
If the wrong printer is selected, choose the correct one and test again.
In Windows 11, installed printers can be viewed under Settings, Bluetooth & devices, Printers & scanners.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot offline printers
link.description: Includes checking and selecting the correct default printer in Windows.

selectCorrectPrinter.title: Select the correct printer
body: Select the correct physical printer in the application's Print dialog.
Send the document again.
If the printer is used regularly, consider setting it as the Windows default printer.
If the printer still does not print, restart this guide and continue with the print queue checks.

checkPrintQueue.title: Check the Windows print queue
body: Open Windows Settings, then Bluetooth & devices, then Printers & scanners.
Select the affected printer and choose Open print queue.
Look for stuck, paused, failed or pending jobs.
Check that the printer has not been paused.
A stuck print job can prevent newer documents from printing.

link.name: Microsoft: View the print queue
link.description: Instructions for opening and examining the Windows print queue.

checkPrintQueue.alt: Windows printer settings showing the Open print queue option
checkPrintQueue.caption: Open the print queue for the affected printer to check for pending or stuck jobs.

clearPrintQueue.title: Clear stuck print jobs
body: Open the affected printer's print queue.
Cancel any stuck or failed documents.
Resume the printer if printing has been paused.
Be careful when clearing a shared printer queue because other users may have jobs waiting.
Try printing one small document after clearing the queue.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix stuck print jobs
link.description: Official instructions for cancelling stuck jobs and restoring the print queue.

clearPrintQueue.alt: Windows print queue showing the Cancel command for a print job
clearPrintQueue.caption: Cancel stuck jobs before sending a new test document.

restartPrintSpooler.title: Restart the Windows Print Spooler
body: Restart the computer first if this is a simple home or small-office setup.
If printing still fails, press Windows + R, enter services.msc and press Enter.
Find Print Spooler in the Windows Services list.
Right-click Print Spooler and select Restart.
Restarting this service can interrupt other active print jobs, so take care on shared or managed computers.
Send another test document after the service restarts.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix Print Spooler problems
link.description: Official instructions for restarting the Print Spooler service.

restartPrintSpooler.alt: Windows Services console with the Print Spooler service highlighted
restartPrintSpooler.caption: The Print Spooler service manages print jobs in Windows.

checkPrinterConnection.title: Identify the printer connection type
body: Determine how the printer communicates with the computer.
A USB printer connects directly to the computer using a cable.
A network printer may use Wi-Fi, Ethernet or a shared connection through another computer or print server.
Select USB for a directly connected printer, or Network for the other connection types.
Check the connection before reinstalling drivers.

checkUsbConnection.title: Check the USB printer connection
body: Confirm the USB cable is firmly connected to the printer and computer.
Try another USB port on the computer.
Avoid USB hubs and docking stations while testing.
If possible, try another known-working USB printer cable.
Allow Windows a moment to detect the printer after reconnecting it.

replaceUsbCable.title: Replace or reconnect USB cable
body: A loose or damaged USB cable can prevent printing.
Reconnect the printer directly to the computer.
Try a known-working cable and USB port.
If Windows now detects the printer, try printing again.
If the printer remains undetected, continue investigating the printer's USB interface and driver.

checkPrinterDetected.title: Check whether Windows detects the printer
body: Open Settings, Bluetooth & devices, Printers & scanners.
Confirm the printer appears in the installed devices list.
If it is missing, check whether Windows recognises the USB device.
A missing printer may indicate a connection, USB, driver or printer hardware issue.

checkNetworkPrinterConnection.title: Check the printer's network connection
body: Confirm the printer is connected to the correct network.
For Wi-Fi printers, check the wireless network name and connection status on the printer.
For Ethernet printers, check the network cable and link lights.
For printers shared from another computer, check that the host computer is powered on and accessible.
Guest Wi-Fi networks and client isolation can prevent computers from reaching printers even when both have internet access.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection problems
link.description: Official troubleshooting instructions for USB, network and wireless printer connections.

reconnectPrinterNetwork.title: Reconnect the printer to the network
body: Reconnect the printer to the correct Wi-Fi network or Ethernet connection.
For shared printers, confirm the host computer and printer-sharing service are available.
Use the printer manufacturer's network setup instructions if required.
Once connected, try printing again.
If the problem persists, continue checking the printer's IP address.

checkPrinterIp.title: Check the printer's IP address
body: View the printer's network settings or print its network configuration report.
Check that it has a valid IP address appropriate for the local network.
An address beginning with 169.254 may indicate that the printer has not received an IPv4 address from DHCP.
Check whether the printer's IP address has changed since it was installed.
On the computer, check the installed printer's Port settings where applicable, and confirm they point to the correct printer address.
Where appropriate, use a DHCP reservation to keep the printer's address consistent.

restartPrinterRouter.title: Restart the printer and check network addressing
body: Restart the printer and allow it to reconnect to the network.
Check whether it receives a valid IP address.
If several network devices have connection problems, investigate the router's DHCP service and consider restarting the router.
Avoid restarting the router unnecessarily if other users depend on it.
Try printing again once the printer is connected.

checkPrinterOnlineStatus.title: Check the printer's online status
body: Open Windows Settings, Bluetooth & devices, Printers & scanners.
Select the affected printer and check its status.
If Windows reports Offline even though the printer is ready, the saved connection may be stale.
For network printers, check whether the printer IP address has changed.
Also check whether Windows is configured to use the printer offline.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot offline printers
link.description: Official steps for restoring an offline printer in Windows.

disableUsePrinterOffline.title: Disable Use Printer Offline
body: Open the print queue for the affected printer.
Find the option named Use Printer Offline, if available, and make sure it is disabled.
Also check that printing is not paused.
The location of this setting varies between Windows versions and printer interfaces.
If the printer remains offline, verify its network connection and saved printer port.
Try printing a test page.

link.name: Microsoft: Offline printer troubleshooting
link.description: Instructions for checking Windows printer status and restoring printing.

printTestPage.title: Print a Windows test page
body: Open Windows Settings, Bluetooth & devices, Printers & scanners.
Select the affected printer.
Open Printer properties and choose Print Test Page, or use the available Test Page option.
A Windows test page helps separate printer connectivity problems from issues with the original document or application.
If the test page prints, investigate the original application or document.
If it fails, continue checking the printer driver and installation.

link.name: Microsoft: Printer connection and printing problems
link.description: Windows troubleshooting instructions including printing a test page.

documentOrAppIssue.title: Document or application issue likely
body: The Windows test page prints successfully.
The problem may be with the original document, application or its print settings.
Try printing a simple document from another application.
Check the selected paper size, print range and printer preferences.
If necessary, save the original document as a PDF and try printing that.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix printing problems in applications
link.description: Troubleshooting steps for printing failures in Word, Excel and other applications.

checkDriver.title: Check the printer driver
body: Check that Windows is using a driver suitable for the exact printer model.
A generic driver may support basic printing but omit some manufacturer-specific functions.
Driver problems can occur after Windows updates, printer changes or reinstallations.
Check the manufacturer's support website for a current compatible driver.
If the driver is correct but printing still fails, consider removing and re-adding the printer.

link.name: Microsoft: Printer driver troubleshooting
link.description: Official guidance for diagnosing printer connection and driver problems.

installCorrectDriver.title: Install the correct printer driver
body: Find the correct printer driver on the manufacturer's official support website.
Select the exact printer model and supported Windows version.
Install the driver or complete software package as appropriate.
Restart Windows if the installer requests it.
Print another Windows test page.
If printing still fails, continue with printer reinstallation.

reinstallPrinter.title: Remove and re-add the printer
body: Record the printer's current connection method, IP address and any important settings.
Remove the affected printer from Windows Printers & scanners.
Restart Windows if needed.
Add the printer again using USB, network discovery or its confirmed IP address.
Install the correct manufacturer driver where required.
For shared printers, check with the network administrator before changing the configuration.
Print a test page after reinstalling.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection problems
link.description: Instructions for removing, reinstalling and troubleshooting printers in Windows.

testPrintAgain.title: Test printing again
body: Confirm the correct physical printer is selected.
Send a simple one-page document to the printer.
If the test document prints, retry the original print job.
If both documents print successfully, the problem is resolved.
If the simple document prints but the original does not, investigate the original document or application.
If the simple document does not print, continue checking the Windows print queue.

finalPrinterEscalation.title: Further printer diagnostics required
body: The printer is powered on and ready, but the computer still cannot print after queue, connection and driver troubleshooting.
Test from another computer if available to establish whether the problem affects one device or several.
Check printer firmware and manufacturer support information for the exact model.
For network printers, investigate router isolation, firewall rules, printer ports and print server configuration where applicable.
Record any Windows error messages, printer error codes and results of the tests already performed.
Avoid factory-resetting the printer until important network and configuration settings have been recorded.
If the printer cannot print its own internal test page, investigate the printer hardware rather than Windows.

link.name: Microsoft printer troubleshooting
link.description: Official Windows troubleshooting reference for unresolved printing problems.
